statement: A kangaroo sits at 4 on a number line. Each jump takes it 10 to the right. Where is it after 3 jumps?

choices.misconception: I added 3 to 4 instead of adding three jumps of 10.
I made only one jump of 10 and stopped too soon.
I counted the place it started as the first jump, so I made only two jumps.
I forgot it started at 4 and counted 10, 20, 30 from 0.

hints: Say the numbers it lands on, one jump at a time.
Jumping 10 changes the tens digit by one and leaves the ones digit alone. Start from 4 and count in tens.
From 4, one jump lands on 14 and two jumps land on 24. Make one more jump.

solutions.reliable: Count in tens from 4: 14 after one jump, 24 after two, 34 after three. The idea to keep: adding 10 adds one to the tens digit and keeps the ones digit.

whyOnTest: Counting on in tens from a number that is not a multiple of 10 tests place value on the number line.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
